what_changed_today: MONTE CARLO EDGE DECAYED SHARPLY: adjusted prob_up_first fell to 57.25% (raw 62.25%) from 65.77% prior, with 42.75% down-first, median 4d up vs 7d down and probability_regime 'balanced' — a fourteenth consecutive session failing all regime thresholds (65/70/75), and the up-skew has now given back essentially all of the Aug 7–10 improvement.

SIXTH CONSECUTIVE FAILURE UNDER THE UNCONFIRMED 7,793.68 HIGH, NOW WITH A 20-DAY BREACH: close 7,728.20 (-0.32% vs 7,753.11) is the third straight lower close inside the 7,700–7,794 shelf and price has slipped marginally below a flattening 20-day (~7,748) — the Aug 5 anchor stays 'unconfirmed_new_high' and the shelf increasingly reads as distribution.

MOMENTUM ROLLED OVER FROM THE TOP OF THE RANGE: the 5-day chart shows daily RSI fading from ~63 to ~46-49 and 5-day MFI decaying to ~44 from the ~91 Aug 4 peak at a lower price, while the intraday tape ground down from 7,768 to a 7,716 low and closed in the lower-middle of the range after a failed late bounce.

EXTENSION EASED WHILE VALUATION STAYED CAPPED: +9.46% above the 200-day (from +9.89%) keeps the market at the top of the moderate band, but ERP is still pinned at 0.29% with forward PE 20.09x and the 10-year at 4.684%, leaving the ERP-confirmed re-entry floor at 7,419.56 — 4.0% below spot.

CREDIT AND VOLATILITY REMAIN THE BULL CASE: junk spread tightened again to 1.22 (score 99, year-low shelf) and VIX 15.28 sits below its 50-day MA (~17.2), while McClellan ticked up to 993.76 — improving but still off cycle lows — and net new 52-week highs remain depressed at 1.04.
narrative_summary: Price closed at 7,728.20, down 0.32%, marking the sixth consecutive session trapped beneath the unconfirmed 7,793.68 record high and the first slip below a flattening 20-day SMA — the 7,700–7,794 zone now looks like a distribution shelf rather than a base. Credit and volatility remain unambiguously supportive (junk spread 1.22 at year-lows, VIX 15.28 under its 50-day), and the trend skeleton is intact with the 50-day well above a rising 200-day, but internals continue to lag badly: net new 52-week highs at 1.04, McClellan only just recovering off cycle lows, and 5-day MFI down to ~44 versus ~91 on Aug 4 at a comparable price. With ERP compressed to 0.29% inside the valuation-ceiling band and the Monte Carlo edge decayed to a balanced 57.25% up-first, the setup fails the 70% Late Bull threshold for a fourteenth straight session. Posture stays trim-bias and patient: no adds here, let the 7,610 / 7,554 / 7,497 fib ladder do the work.
open_questions: Does the 7,793.68 swing high ever confirm with a qualifying close above it, or does the six-session 7,700–7,794 shelf resolve downward as a completed distribution top?
Is today's close below a flattening 20-day SMA the start of a genuine regime shift, or noise inside an ongoing consolidation that the rising 50-day absorbs?
Can McClellan's recovery to 993.76 broaden into real participation expansion, or does net new 52-week highs stuck at 1.04 confirm terminal narrow leadership?
Does the year-low junk spread (1.22) continue to validate risk appetite if equity momentum keeps deteriorating, or does credit finally follow equities lower?

rows.signal: Defense and patience — trim into strength, do not chase

confirming_evidence: Trend skeleton fully intact: 50-day SMA 7,500.99 well above a rising 200-day SMA 7,060.26, price +3.03% vs 50-day and +9.46% vs 200-day; the 3-year and 1-year charts show an uninterrupted higher-high/higher-low structure.

Credit confirms equity strength: junk vs investment-grade spread tightened to 1.22 (score 99), the tightest of the year and clearly below its recent average — no credit warning at all (15_junk_bond_spread.png).
VIX 15.28 sits at the low end of the standard operating regime and below its ~17.2 50-day MA, indicating an orderly, non-stressed tape rather than distribution under duress (13_vix_volatility.png).

Price remains above every Fibonacci retracement level of the 7,313.92–7,793.68 swing (23.6% = 7,680.46), and the 125-day MA at 7,184.20 is far below spot, keeping the intermediate momentum score constructive (09_fear_greed_momentum.png).
McClellan Volume Summation Index has recovered to 993.76 from the ~830 cycle low, the strongest breadth reading in roughly two months (11_breadth_mcclellan.png).
Forward EPS continues to rise (384.63 from 380.33 two weeks ago), so the valuation ceiling is being lifted by earnings rather than requiring price compression alone.
Safe-haven demand at +3.24 (score 67) shows equities still outperforming bonds on a 20-day basis, with no rotation into defensives (14_safe_haven_demand.png).
Put/call 5-day average at 0.71 sits right at its one-year mean — neither complacent enough to be a trim trigger nor fearful enough to be a contrarian buy (12_put_call_ratio.png).

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: McClellan has recovered to 993.76 from its ~830 cycle low, the best reading in two months, suggesting participation is quietly broadening beneath a flat index.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Net new 52-week highs have decayed to 1.04 (score 31) while the index sits within 1% of an all-time high — the narrowest leadership of the advance, and McClellan is still below its Feb/Apr peaks despite record price.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down; headline strength with weak breadth indicates narrow leadership.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Daily MFI on the 1-month/3-month charts is still holding in the mid-60s and RSI near 49-63 — well clear of the buy zone, consistent with a normal pause in an uptrend.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: 5-day MFI has collapsed from ~91 on Aug 4 to ~44 today with price at a comparable level, and daily RSI has faded from ~66 to ~46-49 — a multi-session bearish price/momentum divergence confirming institutional bid withdrawal under a flat tape.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Bearish divergence: price makes a higher high while MFI or RSI makes a lower high; MFI falling toward/below 50 during a stall confirms distribution.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Forward EPS keeps rising (384.63) and forward PE at 20.09x is only modestly rich, so an intact uptrend with tightening credit can be held rather than reduced.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: ERP of 0.29% on a 4.684% 10-year sits inside the 0.0%–0.5% valuation-ceiling band; the ERP-confirmed re-entry floor of 7,419.56 is 4.0% below spot, meaning there is no valuation cushion for adds at current price.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: ERP 0.0% to 0.5% = valuation ceiling: trim bias, no aggressive adds. The ERP-confirmed floor defines the re-entry level.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: VIX 15.28 below its 50-day and junk spreads at year-lows say the pullback from 7,793.68 is orderly profit-taking, not the start of a risk event; the rising 50-day at 7,501 is a robust backstop.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: A close below a flattening 20-day SMA after an extended advance is a regime shift, not a normal dip — and it comes with a third consecutive lower close inside a six-session distribution shelf.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: A close below the 20-day SMA after an extended advance is a regime shift, not just a normal dip.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Fear & Greed at 60.80 (Greed) reflects restored risk appetite consistent with an intact bull trend and is far below the 70+ euphoria extremes of Feb 2026.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Greed-zone sentiment at record price with net new highs at 1.04 and momentum rolling over is classic narrow-leadership topping behavior; the index has already ticked down from its ~65 recent peak.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Headline strength with weak breadth indicates narrow leadership; falling sentiment near new highs is a topping warning.

primary_tension: The most supportive credit and volatility backdrop of the entire arc (junk spread 1.22 at year-lows, VIX 15.28 below its 50-day, 50-day above a rising 200-day, price above every fib) is colliding with a six-session failure to extend beneath an unconfirmed 7,793.68 record high that has now produced three consecutive lower closes and a first slip below a flattening 20-day SMA, alongside a multi-session money-flow divergence (5-day MFI ~44 vs ~91 on Aug 4 at similar price), net new 52-week highs stuck at 1.04, ERP compressed to 0.29% inside the valuation-ceiling band, and a Monte Carlo edge decayed to a balanced 57.25% up-first — failing the 70% Late Bull threshold for a fourteenth consecutive session.
